notes.body: Bōya is a fond way to address a small child, usually a boy; here both parents use it for their baby girl.
sources: p2 女の子, p8 坊や

variants.body: Bōya is a fond way to address a small child, usually a boy; here both parents use it for their baby girl. English keeps Bōya and keeps she/her for the child.

Bōya (坊や) is a fond address for a small child, most often a boy. The child is introduced as a girl (p2 女の子) yet both parents call her Bōya here and later. English keeps Bōya capitalised and keeps she/her, preserving the parents' fond usage rather than correcting her into a boy.

notes.body: Here the sound is only wind and rain, unheard in the bustle — the middle step between the storm announced at the start and the storm named at the end.
sources: p1 嵐だ, p8 雨風の音を耳にしない
notes.span: they did not hear the sound of the wind and rain.

variants.body: Here the sound is only wind and rain (p8 雨風の音), unheard in the feeding bustle, distinct from the bare storm (p1, p38 嵐) that frames the evening. It marks the progression: announced, then unheard, then heard alone by the mother, then finally named by the husband.

data.say: Kept one Casual note for Bōya and added one Curious/Student note for the unheard wind-and-rain step in the storm frame; nothing else on this page needs a note.
